name: Uber Technologies
thesis: Uber is a global mobility and delivery marketplace with structural compounding from audience growth, trip frequency, Uber One cross-sell, and operating leverage. The core business thesis is intact, but the holding is on Watch because autonomous vehicles can change distribution economics. Waymo is already a scaled, safety-evidenced direct competitor; Tesla is a credible but less-proven second threat. Uber wins if AV supply remains fragmented and its hybrid network earns an attractive, capital-light take rate. The thesis weakens if Waymo and Tesla keep dense-market demand in direct apps, Uber's AV take rate falls below 10% while it funds guarantees or fleet infrastructure, AV-overlap markets underperform matched controls by more than 5 points for two quarters, or AV capital at risk exceeds $2B / 20% of trailing FCF without contracted returns. The revised DCF now values this fork explicitly: about $96 base, $150 bull, and $30 AV bear; the bear assumes 15% terminal operating margin and a 9x exit rather than preserving current marketplace economics. Position posture: hold around 2.0-2.5%, cap at 3.0% before AV economic proof, add toward 3.5-4.0% only after at least two proof points including one economic proof, and trim toward 1.0-1.5% when an approved warning trigger fires.
key_driver: MAPCs × trips/MAPC × Mobility take rate, constrained by AV routing share, AV contribution profit, and AV capital at risk

tier_3_kpis.current: Waymo has California driverless deployment authorization; Tesla is listed only for testing with a driver in California as of the latest permit page
tier_3_kpis.break_condition: Approved 2026-07-27: re-underwrite when direct competitors obtain commercial driverless approvals materially faster than Uber's non-Waymo partners.

tier_3_kpis.name: Exposure-normalized AV safety and reliability
tier_3_kpis.current: Waymo reports 220.6M rider-only miles through March 2026 and materially lower injury-crash rates versus matched human benchmarks; Tesla does not disclose normalized Robotaxi safety

tier_3_kpis.current: No supplier count meeting the approved scale definition is disclosed

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Approved 2026-07-27: Uber Mobility growth in AV-overlap cities trails matched controls by >5 percentage points for 2 consecutive quarters
Approved 2026-07-27: Waymo ends Uber exclusivity in Austin or Atlanta or materially shifts those cities to its direct app
Approved 2026-07-27: Mobility margin compresses >100 bps YoY as AV volume rises and insurance is not the main cause
Approved 2026-07-27: AV capital at risk exceeds $2B or 20% of TTM FCF without contracted returns
Approved 2026-07-27: AV platform take rate is below 10% while Uber bears material guarantees, incentives, vehicle, or depot costs
Approved 2026-07-27: Waymo and Tesla each reach 5-10% of addressable rides in multiple major overlap cities while Uber is excluded from most of those trips
Driver-classification ruling forcing W-2 in core US states (CA-style spread)
Take-rate compression from regulator caps or competitive intensity
Insurance cost inflation outrunning pricing power

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken. (Universal floor; per-ticker rules below are stricter.)
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

bear_deltas.note: Owner approved 2026-07-29 as the simplified thesis seed for the AV-disintermediation/capital-intensity bear. The live workbook is more precise: near/terminal growth -6pp/-4pp, near/terminal margin -5pp/-8pp, exit -5.5 turns, terminal g -0.5pp, yielding about $30 per share. Margin and multiple compression proxy both lower AV take rates and incremental guarantees, fleet, depot, charging, or other capital support because the scenario schema has no separate capex lever.

business_model_rules.narrative: Trips YoY < 8% for 2Q — core volume metric stalling. Uber has been compounding trips ~15-20% post-COVID; sub-8% means frequency growth and MAPC adds are both decelerating.
Gross bookings cc < 10% for 2Q — the volume × take-rate compounding thesis breaks. Mid-teens is the structural normal.

business_model_rules.kpi_name: Adjusted EBITDA margin (% of gross bookings)
business_model_rules.narrative: Adj. EBITDA / gross bookings < 4.0% for 2Q — operating leverage thesis breaks. Mgmt guides toward continued YoY margin expansion off the ~3.5-4.0% bar; failure to grind higher signals competitive intensity, insurance pressure, or growth-investment overflow.

business_model_rules.kpi_name: Free cash flow margin (FCF / revenue, GAAP)
business_model_rules.narrative: FCF margin < 15% (FCF / revenue) for 2Q — Uber's structural FCF conversion is high-teens once insurance + working-capital normalize; sub-15 means investment cycle is consuming the operating leverage.
